solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stone seat from which one has furthest to rise?

definitions.text: from which one has furthest to rise?

parts.note: stone is rock
seat as in a person's behind, the bottom

explanation.surface: A stone bench so low that anyone sitting on it faces the longest climb back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone seat' reads as one piece of garden furniture, but it splits into two synonyms set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest possible point is, by the idiom, the place from which any recovery has the longest way to go.

clue.text: Naughty drivers close to boundary

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so close to boundary takes its end

explanation.surface: Motorists behaving badly as they near the edge of a field or territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British breakdown and motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy describes something risqué or slightly indecent, a mild synonym for naughty.

clue.text: Queen possibly needing case for garment she's unlikely to wear

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, the possibly marking it as one kind of queen
a case in court is a lawsuit, a suit

explanation.surface: The monarch requires a box or covering for some outfit she would never put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty, but here it is a female cat; the definition then plays on the same cat, who would hardly don a one-piece bodysuit named after her kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece bodysuit is not something a female feline would ever put on.

clue.text: Supporter's complaint, on introduction of northern player

indicators.note: the complaint has a letter introduced into it, so the northern abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
a player is an actor; an actress here

explanation.surface: A backer's grievance arises when a northern performer is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter's' is 'Supporter is', the 's acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives money or help to a cause is its patron, a backer or supporter.

clue.text: Extreme parts in twelfth edition come from such a source

indicators.note: the extreme parts of a word are its first and last letters, taken from each of the three words

explanation.surface: The outermost sections of the twelfth printing are where it all originates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extreme parts in' picks the outer letters of 'twelfth', 'edition' and 'come': TH, EN and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned adverb means from that place or origin, as in springs rising thence.

clue.text: Where to store stuff you formerly dumped in river

indicators.note: one piece is dumped inside the other, so the old pronoun goes into the river

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river
thou is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A place to keep the things you once threw into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed or outbuilding is a handy place for keeping tools and other belongings.

clue.text: Means of dispatching members

definitions.meaning: weapons are the means of killing, or dispatching, someone
limbs of the body are members

explanation.surface: How to send off the people who belong to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weapons used for killing and the upper limbs of the body.

clue.text: Register liable to change again

parts.note: a meter registers or reads a quantity
apt, as in apt to do something, means liable

explanation.surface: An official record that might well be altered once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' looks like a noun, a list, but it is the verb: a gauge reads a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust or modify once more to fit new conditions.

clue.text: Dismissed SA team lamented getting involved

indicators.note: one piece gets involved in, enters, the other, so the weeping goes inside SA

parts.note: taken as written
lamented means wept
a team is a side

explanation.surface: A South African cricket team was bowled out, and their fans grieved as it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South Africa, so the surface reads as a cricket report.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush something off is to reject or disregard it, an idiom for dismissing.

clue.text: Bed salesmen assuming new functions

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: the salesmen assume, take on, the new letter inside them

parts.note: sales agents are salesmen

explanation.surface: Furniture sellers taking on fresh roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Functions' is the mathematical sense, trigonometric ratios.
explanation.definitionFit: The cotangent is a trigonometric ratio, one of the mathematical functions of an angle.

clue.text: Disturb fairies, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for fairies is said aloud and gives a word spelt differently

parts.note: fays is an old word for fairies

explanation.surface: Unsettle the little winged folk, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or fluster someone is to throw them, a close synonym for disturb.

clue.text: Baby bonnet, apparently, in secret storage space

definitions.meaning: jokingly, a hat for a baby under one year old
the idiom for keeping something to yourself, stored secretly in your head

explanation.surface: A baby's hat doubles as a hiding place for secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means kept private, and a jokey reading makes it headwear for an infant under one year.

clue.text: Record held by green worker, a better service provider

indicators.note: the record is held by the green, coming after it

parts.note: a green is a stretch of grass, turf
an account is a record or report
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A record held by a gardener, a superior kind of service supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative, but it is one who bets. A turf accountant is a British euphemism for a bookmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker provides a service to the person placing bets, one who gambles.

clue.text: Academist given extra time to work ground

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A member of an academy is given extra time to finish working on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun, a field, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewed food is ground between the teeth, so chewed means ground.

clue.text: Classical region's key citizen volunteers once, going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: A is a musical key
cit is short for citizen
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force before being renamed

explanation.surface: An ancient area holds the key to old volunteer soldiers heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army, TA, became the Army Reserve in 2014, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica is the region of ancient Greece around Athens.

clue.text: Potentially dangerous mineral like prime salt

parts.note: as means like
prime means best, the top quality
a salt is a sailor, and OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A hazardous mineral resembling top-grade salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' suggests the mineral, but it is an old sailor, an ordinary seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous silicate mineral causes lung disease when inhaled.

clue.text: Fine fencing placed originally on a French pasture

indicators.note: the fine word fences in, surrounds, the letter

parts.note: sheer fabric is fine, thin

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of placed

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: Delicate fencing set on a French meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract of grazing land for flocks of sheep is a pasture.

clue.text: Our opponents adopting main rule of Olympians?

indicators.note: the opponents adopt, take in, the word for main

parts.note: they, the other side, are our opponents
arch means chief or main, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: Our rivals taking up the principal regulation of the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympians' suggests athletes, but means the gods of Mount Olympus, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by gods is theocracy's ancient cousin, and the gods of Greek myth lived on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Gut-wrenching reason for going online?

parts.note: e- is the prefix for online, as in e-mail
a motive is a reason for doing something, here going

explanation.surface: A wrenching reason to log on to the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, an e-motive would be a reason for going online.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotive stirs strong feelings, which is what gut-wrenching describes.

clue.text: Standard of Federation partially raised in tribute

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The flag of a federation is partly hoisted as a mark of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off a hat as a sign of respect is lifting it in salute.

clue.text: No one stands up to support particular sect

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece supports the one above it

parts.note: a particular is a detail or fact

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Nobody gets up to back one specific religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway group within a larger body is a faction, akin to a sect.

clue.text: Heartless orphan presented by the author as "spoilsport"

parts.note: the author of the clue refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the orphan's name

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie is the American comic-strip and musical orphan

explanation.surface: A writer presents an unfeeling orphan as a killjoy character.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie has five letters, so 'Heartless' drops the middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean, ungenerous person who denies others fun is a killjoy, a spoilsport.

clue.text: Reminder of past content expected in Good Friday sermon?

definitions.meaning: a note pointing the reader back to material given elsewhere in a text
a sermon on Good Friday would refer to the Cross of the Crucifixion

explanation.surface: A reminder of earlier matter, as you would expect in an Easter sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a pointer in a text to another passage, and jokingly a mention of the Cross on Good Friday.

clue.text: Rock and roll dance north of the border

definitions.meaning: to sway, rock and roll, is to stagger
north of the border means Scotland, whose lively folk dance this is

explanation.surface: A rock-and-roll dance found in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to stagger and sway, and is also a lively Scottish folk dance.

clue.text: Sentiment for those who perished on Scott's last journey

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Scott's name

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the sentiment written for the dead

explanation.surface: A tribute to the men who died on Captain Scott's doomed final Antarctic expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scott's last journey' suggests the fatal 1912 South Pole trek; 'last' only takes the T from Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is an outing or journey.

clue.text: Local office bar, one entered on a points system?

definitions.text: one entered on a points system?

parts.note: a bank or firm's local office is a branch
a bar is a stripe, a line

explanation.surface: A nearby workplace pub where someone signed up to a loyalty scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' are railway points, the switches that divert a train onto a secondary track.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary railway route is reached from the main track by switching the points.

clue.text: Action man's love captured by Communist in Revolution

indicators.note: revolution turns the whole piece round, reading it backwards
the love is captured by, held inside, the Communist

parts.note: a Red is a Communist
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A man of action's lover is seized by a Communist during a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts rather than talks is a doer, a person of action.

clue.text: "Gutsy" batting twice bagging international a half-century

indicators.note: the doubled word bags, encloses, the international
twice means the word for batting appears two times

parts.note: a batter who is batting is in
a Test is an international cricket match
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half a hundred

explanation.surface: A brave cricketer, in twice, scores fifty in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutsy' suggests courage, but means of the guts, hence the quotation marks. 'Bagging' puts TEST inside ININ.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestinal relates to the bowels, so it literally means of the guts.
